newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria's BBAG denies South African bid talks.
newsitem.headline: Austria's BBAG denies South African bid talks.

text.p: Austrian brewery holding BBAG said reports in Saturday's edition of daily Kronenzeitung of a five billion schilling bid by South African Breweries (SAB) for its Brau Union unit were without substance.
"BBAG rejects this information since it is completely unfounded," BBAG, whose full name is Oesterreichische Brau-Beteiligungs AG, said in a statement.

"The board of BBAG to this date has not had any talks with those or other persons in this matter. SAB has at several times over the past years unsuccessfully expressed its interest in BBAG and units of the BBAG group," it added.

Brau Union controls some two thirds of the Austrian beer market with an annual output of about eight million hectolitres. The group has wide-ranging interests in Hungary and other eastern European countries.
SAB is the world's fourth biggest beer maker and has interests in the Hungarian and Bulgarian market.
BBAG said selling Brau Union would run counter to its business strategy.
"We are convinced that our beer should remain in Austrian hands," it said.
The holding also denied Kronenzeitung's report that Brau Union had called an extraordinary shareholders' meeting for next Tuesday.
Several of Austria's largest companies, among them supermarket chain Billa and bakery group Ankerbrot, have over the past year fallen under foreign control. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 274
